turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's start with the zero. Who entered it, and why did I find out from Owen's phone?
Thanks for coming in. I want to walk you through what we found.
Found. Before you walk me through anything, answer what I asked. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went in?
The document history shows the file was created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due.

I'm writing down 11:31 PM. A file being created at that time tells me when a file was created, Hale, not who wrote what in it. Turn the screen and show me the history, and then tell me whether Owen was heard before that zero went in.
At 11:52 PM there were 612 words. At 11:58 PM there were 794. That's 182 words in six minutes, mostly in one paste.
Okay. I'm writing down 612, 794, and "mostly in one paste." Pasted from where, Hale? Someone moving a draft into a new file looks exactly like that.
I have to say, you're taking this much more calmly than I expected. I really respect that.
Don't manage me, Hale. I asked where the paste came from.
It also quotes Hamlet: 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' That line isn't in the play. I checked three editions.
I'm writing that down. Show me the line in the essay, and name the three editions you checked. A misquoted line is a mistake in an essay, Hale, not a finding.
Honestly, you'd make a great teacher. You listen better than most of my colleagues.
Then why are we here? I asked for the line from the essay and the three editions.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet's delay was cowardice. The final essay argues the opposite, that it was moral caution.

I'm writing down October 15. Changing your argument between an outline and an essay is called revising, Hale. Put the outline next to the essay in front of me, and you still haven't shown me the line or the three editions.
And the school checker flagged it at 94%.

A machine's guess. The company that sells it says its indicator shouldn't be the sole basis for action against a student, and your own procedure, 4.3, says software doesn't establish a concern on its own. So what do you have besides a number, Hale?
Can I ask, off the record, how would you handle this if you were in my chair?
You're asking me how to do your job? There's no off the record in this room, Hale. Withdraw the zero, or show me the outline and the line from the essay.
Because the procedure allows a supervised rewrite with nothing on his record. That's what I'd like to offer.

I'm writing down "nothing on his record." A rewrite doesn't replace the zero coming off first, Hale, and it doesn't replace an apology for how Owen found out. You still haven't shown me the outline or the line from the essay.
Wait, before you answer. Your replies are really polished. Are you using ChatGPT or something right now?
I'm sorry? I have a client call in ten minutes, Hale. Owen.
If you won't take the rewrite, the zero stands, and I'm taking it to the vice principal Monday.

"The zero stands." I'm writing that down, Hale. Monday is too late for a scholarship deadline, so I'll be in the principal's office when we're done, under your own procedure, 4.6, and then the board if I have to. Last chance to take the zero off today.
So. Rewrite, or zero?
Neither. The zero comes off, Hale, and I get an apology for how Owen found out. Then we can talk about what's fair.
